summary: Iteration 4 — full backend + frontend E2E validation of the structural access separation between DACOT staff (hub_users) and restaurant clients (tenant_users). Created /app/backend/tests/test_access_separation.py (35 new tests) and rewrote conftest.py to parse the markdown credential tables (previous conftest regex no longer matched and would silently skip the whole suite). Full suite: 67/67 pytest tests passed (includes regression suites backend_test.py + test_token_refresh.py). Frontend E2E (1440x900) validated client login->/portal, chips ATIVO/INATIVO, 'Abrir' only on active modules, route guards both ways, window.open handoff, logout and staff dashboard. No functional defects found; 2 minor/security observations reported below.

minor.issue: Lockout identifier uses request.client.host, which behind the k8s ingress is the proxy pod IP (observed 10.231.129.137 and .138 rotating). The 5-strike bucket therefore splits across pods, so via the public URL 9 consecutive wrong passwords did NOT trigger 429 (locally on 127.0.0.1 the 6th attempt correctly returns 429). Recommendation: derive the client IP from X-Forwarded-For (first hop) or key the counter by email only.

Backend config is correct (allow_credentials=True, explicit allow_origins). However the preview edge proxy rewrites/handles preflight and returns Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * without allow-credentials. Not an app defect (frontend is same-origin), noted for awareness only — test asserts app config instead.

integration_issues.issue: Portal.jsx fires GET /portal/context in useEffect before the staff->'/' redirect renders, producing two 403 console errors on every staff visit to /portal. Cosmetic only (redirect works), but the fetch should be skipped when user.user_type === 'staff'.

action_items: Optional: skip the /portal/context request in Portal.jsx when the logged user is staff (removes 2 spurious 403s in console).
Optional (security hardening): use X-Forwarded-For for the login brute-force key so the 5-attempt lockout is not diluted across ingress pod IPs.
Doc fix: review request states Cantina Bella Napoli id = 6a916a0576546a69049b99d6; actual seeded id is 6a916a0576546a69049b99dc.
critical_code_review_comments: Authorization design verified as sound: get_current_user re-derives role/tenant from the DB (token 'ut' only routes the collection lookup), and both launch-token endpoints build restaurant_id/role/module server-side — a malicious body {tenant_id, restaurant_id, role:'super_admin'} was provably ignored.
/portal/context response shape is minimal (user/tenant/modules) and leaks no DACOT admin fields (notes, owner, plan, password_hash) — verified by key-level assertions.
server.py is 1043 lines; consider splitting into routers (auth, hub, portal, public) before it grows further.

Temporary: TEST_Restaurante QA tenant (created+deleted in CRUD test), TEST_ notes on Hamburgueria (restored to original 'audit test'), kitchen module deactivate/activate on Hamburgueria (restored active). Module activation state verified back to original: Hamburgueria orders+kitchen, Bella Napoli orders+kitchen, Sushi Zen orders. Test login_attempts and unused reset tokens purged.
test_credentials: /app/memory/test_credentials.md is complete and all 9 accounts (3 staff + 6 restaurant) authenticate successfully; all password hashes are bcrypt $2b$12$.
context_for_next_testing_agent: conftest.py now exposes fixtures: client (super_admin), staff_admin, staff_viewer, client_a_admin, client_a_waiter, client_b_kitchen (restaurant fixtures return (session, login_json)), hamburgueria, bella_napoli, anon, env_backend. STAFF_CREDS/RESTAURANT_CREDS dicts + _login() helper are importable from conftest. test_access_separation.py covers all 16 requested cases (staff read/write scopes, viewer 403 on 7 write endpoints, client 403 on 8 /hub/* endpoints, portal isolation for 2 tenants, handoff claim decoding, public module status, auth playbook). Frontend E2E script covered login redirects, portal chips/buttons, route guards, window.open handoff, logout. Remaining untested: password reset end-to-end (no mailbox), inactive-client login (no inactive seed).
rca_of_the_issue: Brute-force lockout not firing via public URL: _check_lockout keys on f'{request.client.host}:{email}' and behind the ingress request.client.host is the proxy pod IP, which alternates between at least two pods, so consecutive failures land in different 5-strike buckets. Reproduced: 9 public failures -> all 401; same 6 requests against http://localhost:8001 -> 429 on the 6th. Mitigation: parse X-Forwarded-For for the real client IP or drop the IP from the key.
